.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r15/task/tests/scored/*/judge.toml (mode, criterion counts 43/6/3, grep for cross-criterion references and stop wording; line 317 read)
evidence: scoring.toml weights exactly three scored dimensions (functional 0.6, polish 0.2, visual 0.2); all three judge.toml files use mode = "batched". Each scored prompt carries the required instruction. functional/prompt.md:13 "Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure; return a verdict for every criterion. A failed criterion never ends the session.", reinforced by :12 "Never carry a verdict across criteria ... a failure in one must not fail another whose own steps passed", :17 "Fail fast: after two failed attempts at the same control or step, stop and fail that criterion, then continue with the rest" (the stop is scoped to one criterion), :28 "give every criterion its own verdict". polish/prompt.md:12 has the same sentence as functional:13, and :13 "Never carry a verdict across criteria ... Attempt every criterion". visual/prompt.md:15 "Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure or low score; return a score for every criterion ... never carry a score across criteria." The paragraph added in the latest commit (line 7 of each prompt, check only, never fix) ends with "that criterion fails and scores 0; report what you saw and move on to the next criterion" (functional, polish) and "score what is actually on screen with the anchors, and move on to the next criterion" (visual); it is per-criterion and does not introduce a stop-at-first-failure rule. A grep of the three prompts, app_context.md and all scored criteria for stop/abort/skip/remaining/other-criterion wording found no instruction to end the session or to fail a criterion because another failed, and no criterion text refers to another criterion's id or verdict. The only all-or-nothing rule is the global browser gate on line 5 of each prompt ("If the gate fails, assign 0 to every criterion in this dimension"), which is the frozen template's own wording and is a load/type precondition, not a criterion miss. Broken-app probe: an app where Save is dead fails the save criteria, and nothing in the prompts lets that verdict propagate to editor, run or find criteria. Conforming-alternative probe: no wording was found that would zero unrelated criteria of a conforming app after one miss. Notes (not defects): (1) the task prompts drop the template sentence "The global browser gate is the only all-or-nothing rule in this dimension" (template polish:19, visual:49); the fact still holds, but restating it would be harmless hardening. (2) functional/prompt.md:14 "If you run out of budget with criteria unattempted, mark them failed" can zero later criteria on budget exhaustion; that is honest reporting of unattempted work, not stop-on-failure, and belongs to the workload rows. (3) Evidence index: the sixteen scripted-golden artifacts it lists under qc/repairs/coldwater-2026-10-02-strict/ are not on disk at review time (the directory holds only results/build.log and results/restart.log), so their hashes could not be verified; this row rests on static prompt wording and does not depend on them, but the owner should restore or re-index them for rows that do. (4) No configured judge run exists for these bytes, and the earlier hosted Oracle run had no failed scored criterion, so the judge's actual continue-after-failure behaviour is not measured; the private check-batched-independence-wording.py was applied by hand, not executed.
